def transform(grid):
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    # The bottom row encodes two cyclic sequences, split by a gap.
    # For each seed, locate its value in either sequence and extend left/right
    # along the row with the sequence in its displayed order.
    bot=grid[-1]
    runs=[]; cur=[]
    for x in bot:
        if x: cur.append(x)
        elif cur: runs.append(cur); cur=[]
    if cur:runs.append(cur)
    for r in range(len(grid)-1):
        for c,v in enumerate(grid[r]):
            if not v: continue
            seq=next((s for s in runs if v in s),None)
            if not seq: continue
            i=seq.index(v)
            # seed is an anchor at index i; restore full pattern to its left and right
            start=c-i
            for j,x in enumerate(seq):
                if 0<=start+j<len(g[r]): g[r][start+j]=x
    return g
PY

def transform(grid):
    """Copy the matching border template into every isolated marker row."""
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Templates are contiguous nonzero runs on the top and bottom borders.
    templates = []
    for row in (grid[0], grid[-1]):
        run = []
        for value in row:
            if value:
                run.append(value)
            elif run:
                templates.append(run)
                run = []
        if run:
            templates.append(run)

    # An isolated cell anchors the matching template at its corresponding value.
    for r in range(1, h - 1):
        cells = [(c, value) for c, value in enumerate(grid[r]) if value]
        if len(cells) != 1:
            continue
        c, value = cells[0]
        template = next((seq for seq in templates if value in seq), None)
        if template is None:
            continue
        start = c - template.index(value)
        for offset, color in enumerate(template):
            col = start + offset
            if 0 <= col < w:
                out[r][col] = color
    return out
